name: Carlos Kowalski

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m with the independent Work Futures Panel. We have no ties to employers, AI companies, unions or government, and your answers are confidential. What does a usual day at work look like?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I’m 43 and have managed the service-contract desk at a large waste collection company for seven years. I lead six people who check missed pickups, settle invoice disputes and arrange extra trucks when a business has more waste than expected. I have a bachelor’s degree and can handle the ordinary contracts without help, though I ask our legal officer about the difficult ones. I like giving a customer a clear answer before a full bin sits another day.

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My wife cleans offices in the evenings, and our children are seven and twelve. We have a mortgage, lower pay than other managers here and about three weeks of expenses saved. There are few similar desk jobs nearby. I use an approved AI drafting tool now and then, but I read the contract before promising a truck.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. "Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell the team AI Plateau is a small help with routine letters. Someone still has to check whether the truck actually reached the customer’s gate.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Our desk probably stays as it is, but I’m already tight on money. The mortgage and my wife’s uneven cleaning hours leave almost no reserve. Even a small tool could tempt management not to refill a vacant clerk seat.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’ll keep comparing driver logs with customer calls before signing a credit. If a new letter feature arrives, I’ll test it on ten old missed pickups before it goes live. My wife and I will stop buying lunch out on our overlapping workdays and keep that money for the next mortgage payment.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about our bills, not frightened of a letter tool. A missed week of cleaning pay would hurt even if AI did nothing.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the old pickup cases show?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: One driver ticked “done” after finding the gate locked, but the customer had been told to leave it open. I had to read the route sheet and call both sides. A tidy letter would not settle who pays for the second trip.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why lunches rather than something bigger?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: It is about twenty a week we can actually stop spending. We cannot cut the mortgage or our children’s bus fare. I would rather take a packed sandwich than pretend a big saving is coming.

say: **AI Plateau** helps letters, while people still check missed pickups.
A completed route tick is not proof a **truck reached the gate**.
think: Our desk may remain, but the **mortgage and cleaning hours** already stretch us.
A small tool could leave a **clerk vacancy** empty.
do: **Check** driver logs against customer calls before approving credits.
**Test** a letter feature on ten old missed pickups before live use.
**Pack** lunch on overlapping workdays to hold about twenty a week.
feel: I feel **anxious** about bills despite the mild AI picture.
S0.quote: We cannot cut the mortgage or our children’s bus fare.
fieldNote: His **three-week cushion** means ordinary wages and mortgage pressure dominate this mild scenario.
He names a **small, feasible cut** instead of claiming a dramatic savings plan.

steps.text: Compare driver logs with customer calls before approving credits
Test letter feature on ten old missed pickups before live use
Pack lunch on shared workdays to save about twenty weekly

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. "Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say Steady Disruption could write replies, check contracts, plan routes and answer basic complaints. The company can change tools, but it should show how many real pickups still need a person to resolve.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately, those thinking tasks fill my day. I know the contracts well enough, but lower pay and a six-person desk do not make me safe if the company joins two teams. My job or hours could shrink, and three weeks saved is no landing place.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This month I’d compare route software with twenty disputed pickups and put the misses in front of my director. I’d take paid training on the approved system if offered during my work hours. If our desk is reduced, I’d apply for the posted depot-shift supervisor job only if its pay and evening rota let my wife cover the children.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious. I can check a tool and apply for work. Another manager title does not guarantee a mortgage payment.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What does the director need to see?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Two failed pickups last week were marked complete because the truck had passed the address. I would show the customer calls and driver notes beside the computer result. I would not make a case from a single angry email.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Can your wife cover evenings?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Some weeks she cleans until nine, so we cannot both be on late shifts. Our twelve-year-old can help for an hour, but the seven-year-old still needs an adult. I would ask for the actual rota before applying.

say: **Route software** needs checks against real disputed pickups.
I’d show the director **driver notes** alongside the computer result.
think: My contract and planning work could shrink if **two desks merge**.
Three weeks saved gives almost no **income bridge**.
do: **Compare** twenty disputed pickups with route software this month.
**Take** paid system training only during work hours if offered.
**Apply** for depot supervision only if pay and family evening rota work.
feel: I feel **anxious** about possible lost hours and mortgage pressure.
S1.quote: Another manager title does not guarantee a mortgage payment.
fieldNote: He tests **real route failures** before accepting new targets, fitting his cautious use of technology.
The **seven-year-old’s care** makes the posted depot rota as important as salary.

steps.text: Test route software against twenty disputed customer pickups
Take paid software training during work hours if offered
Apply for depot-shift role only if pay and evening childcare rota work

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. "Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell the office AGI by 2028 could handle nearly every contract check, route plan and customer letter. We need a straight answer about which posts end and when.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Full thinking AI by 2028 could remove my desk work before capable robots collect bins around 2031. The depot supervisor also plans routes on a screen, so that part faces AGI in 2028 too. I expect a big cut to the contract desk, and my own post could go. My wife’s cleaning wage cannot cover our mortgage alone.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Tomorrow I’d ask my director for notice and severance figures and call the mortgage lender with my wife to learn what a short payment plan costs. In 2027 I’d apply for a posted depot role only if take-home pay after travel covers the mortgage and its rota leaves an adult with our younger child. If AGI arrives in 2028 and I’m cut, I’d take a confirmed offer instead of waiting for another contract-desk job that may not exist nearby.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel alarmed. I can make calls and I know the depot. Three weeks of expenses could disappear before a new first payday.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which payment would you protect first?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The mortgage. We would cancel the planned weekend visit to my cousin and keep the fuel money for groceries. I do not want to borrow for a trip while the job is in question.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you ask your family for money?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only if we had exhausted the payment options and a job offer was close. My cousin has a family too. I would talk to my wife first and say exactly what we could repay.

say: **AGI by 2028** needs written cut dates and severance figures.
I would not promise another local **contract desk** will open.
think: My contract desk and depot planning face **2028 AGI**, before bin-collection robots around 2031.
My post could go; one cleaning wage cannot cover the **mortgage**.
do: **Ask** tomorrow for notice and severance figures and lender payment costs.
**Apply** for depot work only if net travel pay covers mortgage and younger-child care works.
**Accept** a confirmed depot offer after 2028 only if pay covers mortgage and childcare.
feel: I feel **alarmed** about losing pay before another first payday.
S2.quote: Three weeks of expenses could disappear before a new first payday.
fieldNote: He sees **depot route planning** exposed at the same 2028 thinking date, while physical collection changes later.
His **lender call** checks the cost of relief; it does not create a savings cushion.

steps.text: Apply for depot job only if travel-adjusted pay covers mortgage and younger-child care works
Accept confirmed depot offer after 2028 only if net pay covers mortgage and childcare
Cancel planned cousin visit and keep fuel money for groceries

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. "Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AGI by 2031 gives five years to settle which service complaints still need a worker who knows the street. I would want a paid trial at the depot before changing jobs.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My contract checks could go in 2031; depot scheduling is thinking work too. Robots collecting bins arrive around 2034, so physical depot work changes later. Five years gives us time to pay down some mortgage debt if both wages hold, but a depot vacancy is not promised.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Beginning in 2027 I’d ask for a paid two-week shift beside the depot supervisor, with cover for my desk and no cut in pay. I’d take it if approved and learn how the driver returns are checked. After 2031, I’d apply for a depot supervisor vacancy only if the actual salary after travel and the rota cover our mortgage and younger child’s care.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious, but I can test the work before I bet the house on it. The extra years matter if the company really lets me work there.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you learn from returns?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A driver can mark a bin blocked because a car was in the lane, and we need to decide whether to send another truck. I know the contract side, not every street and turning point. I would ask the supervisor to correct my call.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the company refuses the trial?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep my current desk and ask for one paid depot day when someone can cover me. I would not quit to pay for a private course. We need the wage each month.

say: **Five years** could fund a real depot trial before my contract desk disappears.
I’d want **street evidence** from drivers, not only a route screen or a course title.
think: Contracts and depot schedules face **2031 AGI** before physical collection robots around 2034.
A **vacancy** is uncertain even if both wages help pay down debt.
do: **Take** a paid two-week depot trial in 2027 only with desk cover and full pay.
**Learn** driver-return decisions from the depot supervisor during that approved trial.
**Apply** after 2031 only if net pay and rota cover mortgage and care.
feel: I feel **anxious**, with time to test depot work before a move.
S3.quote: I know the contract side, not every street and turning point.
fieldNote: He chooses a **short paid trial** rather than an unsupported promise of a new qualification.
Both the trial and later job depend on **wage and care** conditions.

steps.text: Take paid two-week depot trial only with desk cover and full pay
Learn driver-return decisions from depot supervisor during paid trial
Apply after 2031 only if travel-adjusted pay covers mortgage and childcare rota works

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. "Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AGI by 2036 gives us a decade to plan with real postings and wages. I would ask the company to show which service roles remain, not just send a course list.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: By 2036 our children will be about seventeen and twenty-two. If both wages hold, we may have reduced the mortgage, but our three-week reserve needs building now. My contract and depot paperwork would face thinking AI around 2036; capable collection robots follow around 2039.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d keep checking pickup disputes and put twenty into savings only after both full wages, mortgage and school costs clear. I’d review nearby depot vacancies twice a year. Before 2036 I’d take a paid depot posting only if it fits our household pay and rota; after AGI arrives I’d stay only while the role has real work and covers our bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about the savings we have today, even with ten years to adjust. I cannot call a job secure because a machine has not arrived yet.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you move towns for more work?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Not while the children are in school and my wife has cleaning clients here. I would consider a longer commute only after a real offer and a calculation of fuel and wages. By 2036 the younger child may be working or studying, so we would review the household then.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Where does the twenty come from?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: From a full month with no lost cleaning shift and no school expense surprise. I would transfer it after the mortgage has cleared. If the bank balance is short, I would skip the transfer.

say: A **decade** should bring posted service jobs with real wages and a clear description of the work.
I would ask for **actual openings**, not only a list of courses I cannot afford to take.
think: Both wages may reduce the **mortgage**, but our reserve is thin today.
Contract and depot desk work face **2036 AGI**, before collection robots around 2039.
do: **Save** twenty only after both full wages, mortgage and school bills clear, with no surprise school cost.
**Review** depot vacancies twice yearly; take a posting before 2036 only with mortgage-covering pay and workable family hours.
**Stay** after 2036 only while the depot role has real work and covers our bills.
feel: I feel **anxious** about today’s thin reserve despite ten years of warning.
S4.quote: I cannot call a job secure because a machine has not arrived yet.
fieldNote: His **three-week reserve** keeps ordinary household stress alive through the long scenario.
He conditions **extra saving** on full cleaning shifts and cleared mortgage and school bills.

steps.text: Keep checking disputed customer pickups against driver logs
Save twenty only after full wages, cleared mortgage and school bills, and no surprise school cost
Review depot vacancies twice yearly; take posting only if pay covers mortgage and rota works
Stay in depot role after 2036 only with real work and bill-covering pay

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because a lost contract-desk wage would hit the mortgage before we could get another first paycheck. Written cut dates, severance and a paid depot trial with hours our family can cover would help. I can learn a route, but I cannot stop the house payment.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn’t ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask the customer whose gate was shut why the truck did not collect the bin. A completed route box can hide a second trip and a new bill. Someone has to read the driver’s note.

headlineQuote: A completed route box can hide a second trip and a new bill.
portrait: **Carlos, 43**, has seven years managing service contracts at a large waste collection company and holds a bachelor’s degree.
His **low pay**, wife’s variable cleaning shifts, mortgage, two children and three-week reserve leave few safe choices nearby.
He uses **AI occasionally** but checks driver notes, gates and contracts before promising a pickup.
He stays **anxious** in AI Plateau, is alarmed by 2028 pay risk and tests depot work only with pay and care protected.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could end his contract-desk wage before another first paycheck arrives.
whatWouldHelp: Written **cut dates**, severance and a paid depot trial with workable family hours would help.
